title: The Best Second Opinion Is Right Where the Primary Is Wrong: Partner Selection for Selective Span Tagging
abstract: arXiv:2610.37678v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A span tagger that ranks its outputs by risk can defer the riskiest ones to a person, and a second model can sharpen this ranking. Which second model should it be? Partner selection is conditional, not global: the best second opinion is the model that is right where the primary is wrong. abstract: arXiv:2610.37679v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Tool-using language agents are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection, and a growing literature probes model internals to catch unsafe actions before they execute, with sharply conflicting results. abstract: arXiv:2610.37680v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Closing the gap between frontier and smaller language models is usually approached by distillation: fine-tuning the small model (student) on a frontier model's (teacher) outputs, which binds transfer to training compute and leaves the transferred knowledge largely opaque. abstract: arXiv:2610.37681v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large reasoning models have recently demonstrated remarkable capabilities in solving complex tasks, where supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on long chain-of-thought data serves as a crucial foundation for eliciting and enhancing their reasoning abilities. title: Prompt-agnostic Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.37683v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Despite their strong performance, large language models remain highly sensitive to prompt formulation. This issue is typically addressed at inference-time through manual prompt optimization, which introduces overhead and lacks scalability. title: An Introduction to Large Language Models for Scientists and Professionals
abstract: arXiv:2610.37684v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have rapidly become important tools for science, education, medicine, and professional work. Despite their apparent simplicity from the user's perspective, effective and responsible use requires an understanding of how these systems work, what their limitations are, and how their outputs should be evaluated. abstract: arXiv:2610.37688v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Deployed classifiers often act on a prediction only when its confidence clears a threshold and pass the rest to a person. abstract: arXiv:2610.37692v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Users engage with large language models on tasks that are purely objective ("When was Netflix founded?"), purely subjective ("What should I name my child?") or anywhere in-between. abstract: arXiv:2610.37719v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Post-training moves a language model's weights by about a thousandth of their norm and changes its behavior sharply; pretraining moves them by a third and buys a slow drift. Existing placement and replication methods redistribute this workload, yet additional expert copies compete with token-related buffers for limited GPU memory. title: ThinkJev: One Thought, Every Budget for Calibrated Typed Decisions
abstract: arXiv:2610.37732v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Many uses of language models end in a typed decision: a choice among a closed set of options, whose probabilities code can act on. abstract: arXiv:2610.37739v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown increasing promise in research-level problem solving, yet a comprehensive collection of such problems is still missing, and evaluating them on research-level problems remains challenging. abstract: arXiv:2610.37784v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Measurements of tree diameter at breast height (DBH) are fundamental to forest inventories, but manual surveys across entire stands or regions are impractical. abstract: arXiv:2610.37786v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Web agents require diverse, executable, and resettable website environments for reproducible training and evaluation. abstract: arXiv:2610.37788v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language model assistants sometimes change a correct answer when the user suggests a wrong one. The behavior, called sycophancy, is usually attributed to preference-based post-training, yet early measurements found it in pretrained models. abstract: arXiv:2610.37796v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent work has hypothesised that large language models may represent some concepts as multi-dimensional manifolds instead of single directions. abstract: arXiv:2610.37809v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM agents that answer questions over Web knowledge graphs are increasingly wrapped in checks derived from the graph's ontology, on the assumption that a formal schema makes a reliable judge. Simulation-ready digital twins require photorealistic rendering across the full FoV and an aligned collision mesh. title: Responsible Quantum Machine Learning for Medical Imaging: A Fairness Audit Across Sensitive Subgroups
abstract: arXiv:2610.37819v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) is increasingly explored for medical classification, yet its behaviour under subgroup-aware fairness criteria remains understudied. We present an empirical fairness audit of classical and quantum classifiers for medical imaging, assuming QML is not inherently fair. abstract: arXiv:2610.37823v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Event cameras, spiking cochleas and similar sensors emit asynchronous events, yet most learning systems first bin them into frames or packets, so the output depends on how the stream was sliced. abstract: arXiv:2610.37830v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI agents can now write software from a plain-English description, but code that runs is not the same as code that does what was asked. This gap matters most for smart contracts, the programs behind Web3 applications that move money on a blockchain and cannot be fixed once deployed. abstract: arXiv:2610.37844v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Computing optimal transport maps between medical images plays a fundamental role in morphological analysis. abstract: arXiv:2610.37859v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language-model agents differ fundamentally from prior intelligent systems in their ability to learn from natural language in context. title: What Constitutes Food Similarity? Visual Representations and Retrieval in Indian Cuisine
abstract: arXiv:2610.37867v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Food similarity underlies retrieval, recommendation, substitution, and other food computing tasks, yet food representations are typically evaluated by identity preservation. title: Human-Residual Steering: Aligning Frozen LLM Judges with Human Judgment Distributions
abstract: arXiv:2610.37868v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used as automated judges, yet most alignment methods target aggregated human judgments and overlook variation among individual annotators. abstract: arXiv:2610.37875v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Accurate AI assistance can improve immediate judgments while reducing opportunities to practise the operations needed for independent performance. title: Interpretable neural equation learning for high-dimensional materials data
abstract: arXiv:2610.37880v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Equation learning seeks to discover compact, interpretable equations from data using various machine-learning techniques. However, few workflows discover and interpret learned equations in sparse, high-dimensional materials datasets. abstract: arXiv:2610.37881v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Deepfake detection models achieve high overall accuracy but exhibit large performance disparities across demographic groups, causing some groups to experience substantially higher false-positive rates than others. title: SAC-GCL: Structure-Aware Compression for Graph Contrastive Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.37898v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Graph Contrastive Learning (GCL) has achieved remarkable success in self-supervised representation learning by maximizing agreement between augmented views of a graph. abstract: One-step and few-step text-to-image generation must accurately render the details specified in the prompt despite limited opportunities for refinement. Distribution matching distillation (DMD) uses score differences to bring the generated distribution closer to a reference distribution. abstract: Interactive world models generate visual content conditioned on user actions, yet maintaining spatial consistency over long-horizon exploration in real time remains challenging. abstract: The hair of stylized characters in games and avatars is built from hair cards: artist-placed ribbons whose geometry is the visible hair, animated by spring bones. title: Glance: The Generator Is Its Own Reranker
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation commonly serves separate models for reranking and answering, duplicating model residency and passage processing. title: EditAgent: Rethinking Agentic Image Editing
abstract: Agentic image editors decompose complex requests into steps, but when a step fails, they mostly retry with the same narrow set of tools and a judge that scores each output by eye directly. abstract: Pixel-space generative Transformers typically use one token per image patch, so capturing finer detail requires more tokens and makes global attention increasingly expensive. abstract: While frontier vision-language models demonstrate strong capabilities in user interface (UI) navigation, their high inference costs prohibit everyday use.
